GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
  
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2750 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 4TH AUGUST, 2026 
PREVENTION OF SOIL DEGRADATION 
 
2750. SHRI JAGADISH SHETTAR:  
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी  
be pleased to state? 
(a) the measures contemplated to prevent the Soil degradation and improper use of manure, 
fertilizers and herbicides by the farmers, which is immensely resulting in the lowest average yield of 
crops in the Country; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAM NATHU THAKUR 
 (a & b)  The Government has taken various measures to prevent soil degradation and promote 
judicious use of fertilizers, manures and herbicides by the farmers as follows- 
(i) Balanced use of fertilizer is promoted under the Soil Health & Fertility Scheme, being 
implemented since 2014-15. Under the scheme, Soil Health Cards (SHCs) are generated which 
provide nutrient status of soil, based on which crop-wise fertilizer recommendations are provided 
to farmers, thereby promoting balanced and efficient nutrient management. SHC helps in 
enhancing crop productivity, reduce cultivation costs, and promote sustainable agriculture. So 
far, 26.09 crore Soil Health Cards have been generated and issued to farmers. 130627 farmer’s 
trainings, 7.17 lakh demonstrations, 7425 farmer’s Melas/ campaigns on soil health card 
recommendations have been organized across the country.  
(ii) National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) was approved by the Union Cabinet on 25 
November 2024.  NMNF promotes chemical-free, nature-based farming practices using on-farm 
inputs. Under the scheme, 23.13 lakh farmers have been registered and 11.44 lakh hectares area 
have been covered,  
(iii) Government has adopted Integrated Pest Management (IPM) as cardinal principle and main 
plank of plant protection in the overall Crop Production Programme since 1985. IPM is an eco-
friendly approach which encompasses cultural, mechanical, biological and need based chemical 

control measures. The Integrated Pest Management-cum-Locust Division of Directorate of Plant 
Protection, Quarantine and Storage (DPPQ&S) promotes Integrated Pest Management (IPM) 
through its 48 Central Integrated Pest Management Centres (CIPMCs) and Locust-cum-CIPMCs 
located across 28 States and 2 UTs. Farmers are trained through Farmer Field Schools (FFS), 
2-day HRD programmes, and safe & judicious use of pesticides awareness programmes. These 
programmes enable farmers to integrate cultural, mechanical and biological control measures. 
(iv) Special awareness Campaign and Khet Bachao Abhiyan  on balanced use of fertilizers have 
been conducted by Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (DA&FW) and ICAR during 
the current Kharif Season 2026 wherein total  2,94,554 programs covering 1,36,73,465 farmers 
have been achieved. During the campaign, farmers have also been made aware on 
Natural/Organic Farming, bio-inputs, alternative fertilizers etc.  
(v) Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) is implemented since 2015-16.  PKVY promotes 
organic farming by providing end-to-end support covering production, processing, certification, 
and marketing. So far, 18.93 lakh hectares have been brought under organic farming and 33.63 
lakh farmers have been benefited. 
(vi) Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) is 
implemented since 2015-16 to promote organic farming in North Eastern States.  So far, 2.36 
lakh hectares have been brought under organic farming and 2.74 lakh farmers have been 
benefited.  
(vii) The Government also promotes Soil Organic Carbon Enhancer namely, Fermented Organic 
Manure (FOM) /Liquid Fermented Organic Manure (LFOM) as a part of judicious use of fertilizers. 
During 2024-25, the annual consumption of FOM/LFOM was 3.36 LMT. During the current Kharif 
Season (1.4.2026 to 16.7.2026), the consumption of FOM/LFOM is 11.86 LMT. 
(viii) Indian Council of Agriculture Research (ICAR) through Directorate of Weed Research, Jabalpur 
is promoting sustainable Integrated Weed Management (IWM) for judicious use of herbicides in 
different crops and cropping systems through research, demonstrations, capacity building and 
extension programmes. The Directorate disseminates scientific advisories through mobile-based 
services, social media, printed literature and village-level extension programmes to promote the 
efficient and environmentally safe use of herbicides. The Directorate is also analyzing the 
herbicide residues in soil and food chain, and accordingly suggesting farmers for crop 
management practices. These interventions have significantly contributed in reducing the 
indiscriminate use of herbicides thereby improving soil health and crop productivity.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2752 
  ANSWERED ON 04/08/2026 
 
INCREASE IN MIGRATION FROM RURAL AREAS 
 
2752. Shri Murari Lal Meena: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether it has come to the notice of the Government that there 
is an increasing trend of migration from rural areas from various 
States and Union Territories in the country due to drought, 
agrarian distress and limited rural employment, if so, the details 
thereof, State and UT-wise; 
(b)  the details of rural labour migration during the last few years, 
State,UT, district and year-wise including Rajasthan and 
especially from Dausa Lok Sabha Constituency; 
(c)  the number of person-days generated under the VB-GRAM-G and 
other rural employment schemes, State, UT-wise along with the 
quantum of benefits accrued to Rajasthan and Dausa therefrom; 
and 
(d)  whether the Government have any special scheme to prevent 
migration, strengthen livelihoods and provide additional 
employment to rural households in drought and agrarian 
distress-affected areas like Dausa and Eastern Rajasthan, if so, 
the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SHRI KAMLESH PASWAN) 
  
(a) & (b): The Ministry of Rural Development is implementing the 
Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Aajeevika Mission (Gramin): 
VB–G RAM G scheme which is a demand-driven wage employment 
programme and seeks to strengthen livelihood security by 
guaranteeing wage employment to rural households while creating 
durable and productive rural assets. The Act provides for one hundred 
twenty five days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year 
to every willing rural household whose adult members volunteer to 
undertake unskilled manual work. The Programme adopts a Whole-of-

Page 2 of 3 
 
Government Approach through convergence with other rural 
development and allied schemes and accords priority to works 
relating to Water Security, Core Rural Infrastructure, Livelihood 
Infrastructure and mitigation of Extreme Weather Events, thereby 
promoting sustainable livelihood opportunities and reducing distress 
conditions that may contribute to migration. The Ministry of Rural 
Development does not maintain data on rural labour migration, 
including migration attributable to drought, agrarian distress or 
limited rural employment.  
  
(c): States/Union Territories-wise details of persondays generated 
under the Mahatma Gandhi NREGS and VB–G RAM G Scheme, during 
the the financial year 2025-26 and 2026-27(as on 31.07.2026) 
including Rajasthan and Dausa district are given at Annexure. 
 
(d): The VB–G RAM G Scheme contains comprehensive provisions to 
strengthen rural livelihoods and generate additional employment in 
areas affected by drought, agrarian distress, natural disasters and 
other extraordinary circumstances. The Programme accords priority 
to Livelihood Infrastructure Works for promoting agriculture and 
allied activities, strengthening self-employment opportunities, 
enhancing rural enterprises and creating durable livelihood assets, 
alongside works relating to water security, climate resilience and 
natural resource management. 
  
Climate resilience and adaptation have been embedded as core 
priorities under the Programme. The Schedule to the Act includes a 
dedicated thematic category on "Special Works to Mitigate Extreme 
Weather Events and Disaster Preparedness", with a focus on disaster 
risk reduction, climate adaptation and protection of rural 
communities and assets from floods, cyclones, storms, droughts, 
landslides, forest fires and other extreme weather events. Illustrative 
works under this category include cyclone and flood shelters, 
disaster-resilient community infrastructure, embankments and 
diversion channels, and water bodies for flood management, 
restoration of rural infrastructure damaged by disasters, and forest 
fire management works. These provisions collectively promote 
climate-resilient villages, sustainable rural livelihoods and enhanced 
employment opportunities, thereby helping to reduce distress 
migration.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2753 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 04TH AUGUST, 2026 
 
PROGRESS OF AGRISTACK INITIATIVE 
 
2753.   SHRI ADITYA YADAV: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण मंũी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the current operational status and rollout progress of the AgriStack initiative and the 
creation of the digital Farmers' Registry across the country, State/UT-wise and district-wise 
for Uttar Pradesh;  
(b)  the total number of unique digital Farmer IDs generated so far against the target of 
covering 11 crore farmers and the time by which all agricultural plots and land records will 
be fully synchronized with this registry;  
(c)  the specific ways in which this digital database is being integrated with existing 
welfare schemes like PM-KISAN, the Jan Samarth platform for Kisan Credit Card (KCC) 
loans and MSP- based crop procurement to assist small and marginal farmers; and  
(d)  the concrete steps and data privacy mechanisms established by the Government 
including the role of the Consent Manager to safeguard farmers' personal and land data 
from unauthorized access or misuse by private tech entities? 
                                                 
ANSWER 
 
   MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
 
   कृ ͪष एवं ͩकसान कãयाण राÏय मंğी (SHRI RAMNATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) & (b): AgriStack is the farmer-centric Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) built as a public 
good for efficient, easier and faster service and scheme delivery to the farmers. It provides 
a comprehensive profile of every farmer, such as farmer’s details, land records, crops grown, 
and assets such as livestock and fisheries. It consists of three foundational registries 
associated with the agriculture sector, i.e., Farmer Registry, Geo-Referenced Village Maps 
and Crop Sown Registry, all created and maintained by the State Governments/ Union 
Territories.  
  

   
        Farmer ID is created by synchronizing farmers' details with their digitized land records. 
As of 30th July, 2026, more than 10.28 Crore Farmer IDs have been created including more 
than 2.46 crore farmer IDs in Uttar Pradesh. The state-wise Farmer IDs generated in the 
country are given in the Annexure -I. The district-wise generated Farmer IDs in Uttar 
Pradesh is given in Annexure –II.  
 
      Further, during Rabi 2025-26, the Digital Crop Survey (DCS) was conducted in 648 
Districts covering more than 31.3 crore plots across the country.  
 
(c): The Farmer Registry created under AgriStack is designed to serve as a foundational 
database for the efficient, transparent and faster delivery of agricultural services. Farmer 
Registry is being integrated with various farmer-centric schemes and digital platforms, 
including PM-KISAN, the Jan Samarth platform for Kisan Credit Card (KCC) loans, and 
MSP-based crop procurement systems to enable service delivery to farmers, particularly the 
small and marginal farmers. 
 
(d): The State Farmer Registry is built in a federated manner, which means the ownership 
of the data is with the respective States. The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare 
has developed the Agri Stack in accordance with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 
2023 and the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules 2025, to ensure the complete privacy 
of farmers' data by ensuring that farmers' data is collected only with their consent and 
farmers have full control over their data for sharing with authorized entities for specific 
purposes. Further, the security features of AgriStack, are fully compliant with the 
cybersecurity guidelines of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) 
and the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In). AgriStack maintains 
farmers' information in an encrypted manner so that only the authorized systems can read 
it.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2754 
FOR ANSWER ON 04.08.2026  
 
 
RECRUITMENTS IN NMDC AND NMDC STEEL LIMITED 
 
2754. SHRI MAHESH KASHYAP:  
 
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the total number of recruitments made in the National Mineral Development 
Corporation (NMDC) and NMDC Steel Limited during the last three years, year-wise;  
 
(b) the number of posts on which the youth of Bastar Lok Sabha Constituency has 
been appointed through the said recruitment;  
 
(c) the details of the skill development and apprenticeship programmes being 
implemented for the local youth; and  
 
(d) whether any policy is being formulated to accord priority to the local qualified youth 
in future recruitments? 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE          (SHRI BHUPATHIRAJU SRINIVASA VARMA) 
MINISTRY OF STEEL 
 
(a)&(b): Details of the total number of recruitments made and number of posts 
on which the persons belonging to Bastar Lok Sabha Constituency has been 
appointed in the NMDC Limited and NMDC Steel Limited during the last three years 
is given below: - 
 
Year Total number of 
recruitments made  
Total number of posts on which the 
persons belonging to Bastar Lok 
Sabha constituency has been 
appointed 
2023 254 108

(c)&(d): The Government of India has taken up following skill development and 
apprenticeship programmes for the local beneficiaries: - 
 
(i) Under the Government of India's Skill India Mission (SIM), the Ministry of Skill 
Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) implements skill, re-skill and up-skill 
training through an extensive network of skill development centres/institutes under 
various schemes, namely Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY), Jan 
Shikshan Sansthan (JSS), National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS) and 
Craftsman Training Scheme (CTS) through Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs). 
These schemes are demand-driven, and training centres are established or 
engaged based on requirement.

(ii) NMDC Ltd. implements various skill development initiatives under its CSR 
programme across the Aspirational Districts of Dantewada, Bastar, Bijapur, 
Kondagaon, Narayanpur and Sukma in Chhattisgarh to promote technical 
education and enhance the employability of local youth. Accordingly, NMDC has 
established a Polytechnic College at Dantewada, an ITI at Bhansi (Dantewada), 
and an ITI at Nagarnar (Jagdalpur). During Financial Year 2025–26, NMDC, in 
collaboration with CIPET, provided skill development training to local youth from 
Dantewada and Bastar, and also sponsored tribal students in medical technology 
and allied healthcare courses. 
 
(iii) The National Institute of Secondary Steel Technology (NISST), established by 
the Ministry of Steel, serves as an industry-oriented skill development and 
technology support centre for the secondary steel sector. NISST regularly conducts 
skill development programmes, technical training and capacity-building initiatives 
for personnel engaged in the secondary steel industry. The training covers 
specialised areas such as Industrial Safety, Quality Improvement, Energy 
Efficiency, Scrap Segregation and Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) to enhance the 
technical capabilities of industry personnel.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
DEPARTMENT FOR PROMOTION OF INDUSTRY AND INTERNAL TRADE 
 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2755. 
           TO BE ANSWERED ON TUESDAY, THE 04TH AUGUST, 2026. 
 
GI TAG FOR RAJAMUDI RICE 
 
2755.  SHRI SHREYAS M PATEL: 
 
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state: 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्री 
(a)  whether the Government has received any application or proposal for 
registration of Rajamudi rice of Hassan district, Karnataka, as a Geographical 
Indication (GI) under the Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and 
Protection) Act, 1999; 
 
(b)  if so, the details of the application, including the applicant, date of filing, present 
status and the reasons for any delay in registration; 
 
(c)  whether the Government has undertaken any study to assess the uniqueness, 
historical significance, traditional cultivation practices, and commercial potential 
of Rajamudi rice for Gl registration; 
 
(d)  whether the Government proposes to extend technical or financial assistance 
to farmers, producer organizations, research institutions, or the Government of 
Karnataka for obtaining the  Gl tag and promoting Rajamudi rice in domestic 
and international markets; and 
 
(e)  the measures taken by the Government to protect, promote, brand, and 
enhance the market value and export potential of Rajamudi rice cultivated in 
Hassan district? 
 
ANSWER 
 
वाणिज्य  एवं उद्योग मंत्रालय में राज्य मंत्री (श्री णिणिन प्रसाद)   
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMERCE & INDUSTRY 
(SHRI JITIN PRASADA) 
 
(a) & (b): Geographical Indications Registry has not received any application for 
registration of Geographical Indications “Rajamudi Rice” grown in Hassan 
District of Karnataka. 
(c): Visvesyaraya Trade Promotion Centre, (VTPC), under the Department of 
Industries & Commerce, Government of Karnataka being the Nodal agency for 
Geographical Indications for the State of Karnataka, commissioned a feasibility 
study through Ramaiah Centre for Intellectual Property Rights (RCIPR), 
Bengaluru, to assess the potential for filing a Geographical Indication 
application for Rajamudi Rice. The study examined aspects relevant to Gl 
registration, including the product's distinctiveness and traditional significance. 

Further, the Department of Agriculture, Govt. of Karnataka has taken up 
Rajamudi Rice under the Desi Thali Scheme, and the product is currently 
undergoing field trials under the supervision of the University of Agricultural 
Sciences, Bengaluru, to generate the requisite scientific and technical data. 
(d) & (e): Government has undertak en various measures for promoting manufacture, 
marketing, sale and trade of Geographical Indication (GI) tagged products 
across the country, including products from Karnataka. These initiatives and 
schemes are implemented uniformly nationwide, ensuring that GI producers in 
Karnataka enjoy equal benefits alongside producers from other States and 
Union Territories. Details of such measures taken by the government are 
placed under Annexure-I. 
 
 
 
********* 
  

ANNEXURE-I 
ANNEXURE REFERRED TO IN REPLY TO PARTS (d) & (e) OF THE LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2755 FOR ANSWER ON 04.08.2026. 
i. Facilitation of GI Registration: The GI Registry provides continuous 
handholding support to applicant associations and authorised bodies 
throughout the GI registration process, i ncluding assistance in addressing 
deficiencies in applications and ensuring compliance with the provisions of the 
Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act,  1999 
and the Rules framed thereunder. Further, vide notification dated 03.11.2025, 
the fee payable for filing GI applications and related proceedings has been 
reduced by 80 per cent, making GI protection more aﬀordable for artisans, 
farmers, producer organisations and traditional communities. 
ii. Support under the MSME Innovative S cheme: Under the Intellectual 
Property Rights (IPR) component of the MSME Innovative Scheme, the 
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises provides consultancy 
services, Intellectual Property facilitation and awareness programmes relating 
to Intellectual Property Rights, including Geographical Indications. The 
Scheme provides reimbursement of 100 per cent of the actual expenditure 
incurred for registration of a GI, subject to a maximum ceiling of ₹2 lakh per 
registered GI, includin g expenses towards professional fees, Government 
fees, preparation of applications, prosecution, hearings, GI logo design, 
laboratory testing and other incidental expenses. The applicants are also 
provided end-to-end support through Intellectual Property Facilitation Centres 
(IPFCs). Further, the Ministry has organised 25 GI Mahotsavs across different 
States to provide market access to authorised GI users, sanctioned 164 
programmes under the One District One GI (OD-OGI) initiative, and facilitated 
participation of GI producers in international exhibitions to enhance exports 
and global visibility of GI products. 
iii. Market Access and Promotion by DPIIT: DPIIT has undertaken several 
initiatives for enhancing the visibility and marketability of GI products, including 
organisation of India GI Fair, GI Mahotsav, GI Pavilions at national and 
international exhibitions, participation in AAHAR, India International  Trade 
Fair, World Food India, Tribal Business Conclave and international trade fairs 
such as Autumn Fair (United Kingdom) and Bazaar Berlin (Germany). 
Promotional activities have also been undertaken through documentaries, 
television campaigns, National Geographic, History TV18, Ma sterChef India, 
social media campaigns, airport and Delhi Metro branding, GI Samagam, GI 
Catalyst Summit and promotion of GI products during the India AI Impact 
Summit 2026. These initiatives are intended to improve awareness, branding, 
market access and export potential of GI-tagged products. 
 
The various promotional initiatives and schemes are implemented uniformly 
across the country, and GI producers from Karnataka are eligible to avail 
themselves of the benefits provided under these schemes and promotio nal 
programmes on an equal basis with producers from other  States and Union 
Territories. The details are as follows:- 
 

Year Initiative Details

Three-day event organised at India Expo 
Centre & Mart, Greater Noida for promotion and 
marketing of GI products.

Week-long event organised at Trade

knowledge sessions for GI stakeholders.

2022)

Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE be pleased to state:  
(a) the minimum support price (MSP) fixed for jute and Paddy for the current year; 
(b) the arrangement made/steps taken for timely procurement in West Bengal; and 
(c) the steps taken to ensure that farmers receive payment directly in their bank 
accounts within the stipulated time?

MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE  
क ृ िष एवं िकसान कʞाण राǛ मंũी (SHRI RAM NATH THAKUR) 
 
(a) to (c): Every year, Government fixes Minimum Support Prices (MSPs) for 22 
mandated agricultural crops including Paddy & Jute for the country as a whole, based 
on the recommendations of the Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices (CACP), 
after considering the views of the State Governments and Central 
Ministries/Departments concerned. 
      The Union Budget for 2018-19 had announced the pre-determined principle to 
keep MSPs at levels of at least one and half times of the cost of production. 
Accordingly, Government had increased MSPs for all mandated Kharif, Rabi and other 
commercial crops with a minimum margin of 50 percent over all India weighted 
average cost of production from year 2018-19 onwards. The details of current MSP of 
Paddy & Jute for Marketing Season 2026-27 are given as under:

Paddy        (Common)   2441 
(Grade A) 2461 
Jute 5925 
 
Out of the total production, only marketable surplus is available for procurement 
by Government agencies when market price of these produce falls below the MSP. 
Government procures cereals and coarse cereals through Food Corporation of India 
(FCI) and other designated State Agencies to provide price support to the farmers. 
Procurement of pulses, oilseeds and copra is done under Price Support Scheme under 
umbrella scheme of Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay Sanrakshan Abhiyan (PM-
AASHA), on the request of the concerned State Government as per the guidelines as 
and when market price of these produce fall below the MSP. Procurement agencies 
under PM-AASHA Scheme are National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing 
Federation of India Ltd (NAFED) and National Co-operative Consumers' Federation of 
India Ltd. (NCCF). Cotton and Jute are also procured by Government at MSP through 
Cotton Corporation of India (CCI) and Jute Corporation of India (JCI), respectively. 
 Increased MSP has benefited farmers of the country including farmers of West 
Bengal which are evident from data of procurement and MSP amount paid to the 
farmers. The procurement details for All India and West Bengal, along with the MSP 

amount paid to farmers during the period 2014–2026 (up to June 2026), are furnished

Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether the Government has reviewed the loss of lives and property 
caused by heavy rainfall, cloudbursts, landslides, and flash floods in hilly 
states, especially Himachal Pradesh, during the last three years and if so, 
the State-wise and district -wise including of Himachal Pradesh during the 
last three years;  
 
(b) the number of persons killed, missing and injured, damaged houses, 
roads, bridges, agriculture, horticulture and public infrastructure along with 
the estimated economic loss during the said period;  
 
(c) the details of the financial assistance sanction ed and released by the 
Central Government, State -wise and the assistance received by Himachal 
Pradesh during the said period;  
 
(d) whether the Government has formulated any special action plan or a new 
scheme for hilly states towards strengthening disaster risk reduction, early 
warning systems, monitoring of landslides and cloudbursts, river 
management and climate -resilient infrastructure and if so, the details 
thereof; and  
 
(e) the concrete steps taken or proposed to be taken for the prevention and

MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS

(a) to (c): As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the 
primary responsibility for disaster management, including disbursal of relief

The State Governments undertake relief measures in the wake of natural 
calamities, from the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) already placed at 
their disposal as well as other available resour ces, in accordance with 
Government of India approved items and norms.   The Central Government 
supplements the efforts of the State Governments and provides requisite 
logistics and financial support.  In the case of disaster of a 'severe nature', 
additional financial assistance is provided from the National Disaster 
Response Fund (NDRF) on the basis of the recommendations of the Inter -
Ministerial Central Team (IMCT), in accordance with the prescribed 
procedure. 
This Ministry does not centrally maintain data regarding the loss of lives and 
property due to any disaster in the country.  However, the details of damages

(d) and (e): The Central Government has taken several initiatives to 
strengthen disaster risk reduction and enhance resilience in hilly States, 
including Himachal Pradesh, under the existing institutional and policy 
framework; as per the details provided below : - 
i. The National Disaster Management Plan (NDMP) and the guidelines 
issued by the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) cover 
disasters such as landslides, cloudbursts, Glacial L ake Outburst 
Floods (GLOFs), forest fires and earthquakes, to which the Himalayan 
region is particularly vulnerable.  
ii. The Government has approved the National Landslide Risk Mitigation 
Project (NLRMP) for implementation in 15 States, including Himachal 
Pradesh, with the objective of reducing mortality and economic losses 
by reducing the vulnerability of communities and their assets to 
landslides. Under the project, a Central share of ₹125.00 crore and 
State share of ₹14.00 crore have been approved for Himachal Pradesh.  
iii. To adopt various structural and non-structural mitigation measures for

Pradesh, Sikkim and Uttarakhand.

Scheme).

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

FUNCTIONING OF KRISHI VIGYAN KENDRAS 
 
2758.  SHRI MANSUKHBHAI DHANJIBHAI VASAVA: 
 
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE कृषि और ककसान कल्याण 
मंत्री be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether the functioning of Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) is being monitored/reviewed in  
the country; 
(b) if so, the State-wise details thereof along with the outcomes recorded during the last three 
years; 
(c) the names of the centres where irregularities have been identified; and 
(d) the corrective steps taken by the Government in this  regard? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR AGRICULTURE AND FARMERS WELFARE 
कृषि और ककसान कल्याण राज्य मंत्री (SHRI BHAGIRATH CHOUDHARY) 
 
(a) & (b): Yes. The functioning of Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) in the country  is 
monitored/reviewed regularly. There is a strong mechanism for monitoring and review of KVKs 
to make them vibrant and effective institution of technology transfer at district level. Monitoring 
and review of KVKs are done regularly at National, Zonal, Sta te and District level by Indian 
Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR); Agricultural Technology Application Research Institute; 
Agricultural Universities and Scientific Advisory Committee of each KVK, respectively. The 
performance and working of KVKs is a lso reviewed periodically by Quinquennial Review Team 
(QRT) and Third Party. 
 
 The latest performance evaluation of KVKs was carried by NITI Aayog in the year 2025 -
26. The report advocates the KVK network as the country’s largest and most decentralized public 
agricultural extension system. The KVKs have a strong institutional framew ork with clear 
mandates, having district -level presence and thus highly effective in addressing farmers’ 
technological needs. About 91% of farmers adopted new practices or technologies promoted by  
 

2 
 
 
 
 
KVKs, indicating that KVK trainings and advisories encourage successful adoption. KVKs 
provide trusted and scientifically sound advisories on crop management, pest and disease 
control, input selection, and climatic risk management through technology valida tion, 
dissemination, and transfer. Their close collaboration with state agriculture departments and 
allied agencies strengthens extension services through demonstrations, training, and capacity -
building initiatives. Additionally, farmers widely trust KVK a dvisories and quality seeds and 
planting materials, resulting in greater adoption of improved agricultural practices and enhanced 
crop performance. 
 
Followings are some major outcomes of the efforts of KVKs during last three years: 
• Conducted 9.67 lakh Frontline Demonstrations (FLDs) on farmers' fields to showcase the 
production potential of improved farm technologies and promote their adoption by farmers. 
• Trained 62.35 lakh farmers including rural youth and 5.06 lakh extension personnel for 
updating their knowledge and skill. Created awareness on improved agricultural technology 
among 826.61 lakh farmers and other stakeholders through a large number of exte nsion 
programs. 
• For catalyzing technology adoption through critical resources, KVKs produced 5.95 lakh 
quintal quality seeds of improved varieties of various field crops and 1518.90 lakh planting 
materials of different horticultural crops. 
• The significant reduction in fire incidents, especially in Punjab and Haryana (both by 95% 
between 2020 and 2025), underscores the success of awareness, technological interventions, 
and policy convergence facilitated by KVKs under Crop Residue Management initiative. 
 
(c) & (d): The financial & administrative irregularities have been identified in five KVKs 
established in the districts viz Sehore, Vidisha, Auriya, Guntur and Thanjavur during the last five 
years. The remedial action has been taken and KVKs in these districts have been withdrawn 
from the concerned Host Organisations.

early maturing- short duration varieties under the National Seed Reserve (NSR) framework, 
activation of contingency seed reserves before monsoon onset and seed quality and 
quantity monitoring during peak demand. 
District Agriculture Contingency Plans have been updated for 342 districts by ICAR – 
CRIDA and State Governments collaboratively. These plans included crop strategies for 
delayed monsoon onset, as well as contingency measures to address mid-season and 
terminal drought conditions.  
Further, the ICAR has developed Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for KVKs 
to implement these contingency plans. These SOPs encompass development of need 
based contingency plans, implementation procedures, coordination with agriculture 
department and other line departments, release of real time agro-advisories for the district, 
capacity development, awareness generation and real time feedback.   
As per the National Policy on Disaster Management (NPDM), the State 
Governments are primarily responsible for providing necessary relief measures on ground 
level in the wake of notified calamities. The State Governments undertake relief measures 
in the wake of natural calamities from funds available in the form of the State Disaster 
Response Fund (SDRF) in accordance with the Government of India approved items and 
norms. Additional financial assistance, over and above SDRF, is considered from the 
National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as per laid down procedure, in case of disaster 
of ‘severe nature, which includes an assessment based on the visit of an Inter-Ministerial 
Central Team (IMCT) and a memorandum submitted by the State for financial assistance 
from NDRF. The financial assistance provided under SDRF and NDRF is by way of relief 
and not for compensation of losses suffered/ claimed. The State wise allocation of SDRF 
/NDRF is available at https://ndmindia.mha.gov.in/.
